VBO:0201106.summary: Lively and expressive, the Pumi tends to be bold in action and a little wary of strangers. It is often vocal, with a restless readiness for work. This Hungarian herding dog’s duties extend to larger livestock, while its well-developed nose and terrier character also found use against rodents.
VBO:0201106.shortDescription: A lively, vocal Hungarian herder with a bold working character and some reserve around strangers.

sources.title: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Pumi standard 56
sources.evidence: Actual FCI56 pp2–3 utilisation/general appearance/temperament supports lively expressive and rather noisy character, boldness, some suspicion toward strangers, restless activity, Hungarian terrier-type herding including larger animals and developed scent/rodent work. pp4–6 supplies square build, long muzzle, upright ears with upper third forward, wide-circle intact tail, tufted wavy/curly coat and accepted intense solid black. Character applies to Pumi generally, not caused by black coat; no suitability/exercise/health guarantees used.

sources.title: Fédération Cynologique Internationale — Pumi nomenclature
sources.evidence: Current FCI exact PUMI56 entry maintains Hungarian breed identity and linked standard; black is an accepted solid coat variety within the breed, not a separate recognized breed.

VBO:0200818.summary: Latvian Hounds tend to be sociable, good-natured and energetic, with a strong hunting drive. They were bred to hunt both small game and hoofed animals, using ground and air scent. After wartime mixing nearly erased the earlier Courland hound, selective breeding established the Latvian Hound in 1971.
VBO:0200818.shortDescription: A sociable, energetic Latvian hound with a strong hunting drive and a history of tracking varied game.

sources.title: Latvian Hound — Latvia Rural Support Service, local preserved breeds
sources.evidence: Actual Latvijas dzinējsuns body read: sociable/good-natured/friendly plus highly energetic/playful/purposeful stronghunting drive; classic hunting of smallgameandhoofed animals; lower/upper scenting discussed in trainedhunting work. Wartimecrossing nearlyerased Courlandhound; selectedbreeding culminated innational1971breed approval. Currentgovernment preserved-breed page supports maintained identity. Exclude family-suitability assertions, guaranteed protection and speculative ancestral breedcrosses.

VBO:0008011.summary: Docile and affectionate, Ca Mè Mallorquins tend to keep close to their handler while hunting at a deliberate pace. This Mallorcan pointing dog searches with its nose at mid-height through uneven ground and dense scrub. Its name, mè, means “lamb” and recalls the nose carriage of a grazing sheep.
VBO:0008011.shortDescription: An affectionate Mallorcan pointing dog known for a measured hunting pace and working close to its handler.

sources.title: Ca Mè Mallorquí — Real Sociedad Canina de España
sources.evidence: Actual temperament section03: docile/obedient/affectionate; utilization deliberatehunting in uneven/thicklyvegetated terrain; nationalGroup11pointingdogtype. Public copy tendencies, no individual obedience or suitability guarantee.

sources.title: Ca Mè Mallorquí — Govern de les Illes Balears, general information
sources.evidence: Actual primary body: deliberate hunting, nose at mid-height like grazingsheep, staysnearhandler, works irregular/densescrub. mè meanslamb and namefollowsnosecarriage. Current regionalbreedclub/registration/selection body establishes maintained identity. Morphology and health/suitability assertions excluded.

VBO:0201210.summary: Gentle with familiar people, Serrano Bulldogs tend to be attentive, steady and courageous. In cattle work, agility is valued for moving beneath stockyard fences. The Brazilian national standard describes cattle handling, guarding and companionship as the breed’s distinct working roles.
VBO:0201210.shortDescription: An attentive Brazilian cattle dog and guardian, described as steady and gentle with familiar people.

sources.title: Buldogue Serrano — CBKC national standard NR11
sources.evidence: Actual standard pp2–3: national Brazilian breed, cattle handling, guard and companion roles; docile/gentle with familiar household people, balanced/attentive/versatile guardian and courageous; agility for passing beneath stockyard fences. No individual safety, temperament or work guarantee. Pages3–5 bind solid agile slightly rectangular morphology, high small semi-drop/drop ears and coiled tail or naturally long straight low tail, all colors. CBKC Group11 is explicitly not FCI recognition.

sources.title: CBKC current breed directory — Buldogue Serrano
sources.evidence: Current primary national directory includes Buldogue Serrano and links its national standard, supporting maintained identity rather than an extinct historical reconstruction. No population count inferred.
